clue.text: Material written about stopping Iron Lady

indicators.note: stopping means the reversed fabric plugs the gap inside the symbol for iron

parts.note: Fe is the chemical symbol for iron

indicators.note: written about means the word for the material is set down the other way round

parts.note: lamé is a fabric woven with metallic thread

explanation.surface: Something written about a fabric that halted Margaret Thatcher, the Iron Lady.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Iron Lady' reads as one phrase, Thatcher's nickname, but the two words are split: Iron belongs to the wordplay and Lady alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A lady is a woman, so she is of the female sex; the noun use names a woman or girl.

clue.text: Girl from island a beauty in recital

indicators.note: in recital means the word is spoken aloud, so only its sound counts

parts.note: a belle is a beautiful woman

explanation.surface: A girl from some island is spoken of as a beauty during a performance.
explanation.definitionFit: Isabel is a female first name, so it fits any girl so called.

clue.text: Fit condition to sail? In short, views err at sea

indicators.note: at sea means confused or all over the place, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone sums up, briefly, that opinions go wrong when out on the ocean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In short' looks like a phrase meaning 'briefly', but its letters are part of the fodder along with VIEWS ERR.
explanation.definitionFit: Seaworthiness is a vessel's soundness for the open sea; the river version is the same quality for inland waterways, the question mark flagging the coinage.

clue.text: Scrubbing of Times inevitable

parts.note: an era is a period of time; here ERA alone supplies the letters
sure in the sense of certain to happen

explanation.surface: A deletion from The Times newspaper is presented as bound to happen.
explanation.definitionFit: An erasure is a rubbing out, and scrubbing something out removes it the same way.

clue.text: Take immense trouble with sell-off — reveal no shilly-shallying

indicators.note: shilly-shallying means wavering this way and that, so these letters are moved around

explanation.surface: Going to great lengths over a sale of assets while refusing to dither about disclosure.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means trying overly hard to please or help, going to great lengths.

clue.text: Emollient sauce on market outside Crown in Ventnor

parts.note: sauce and lip both mean cheek or impudence

indicators.note: outside means the sale word wraps around the picked letter

parts.note: a sale is a market where goods are sold

indicators.note: the crown is the top, so Crown in picks the first letter of the town

parts.note: Ventnor is a seaside town on the Isle of Wight

explanation.surface: A soothing sauce sold at a street market around a seaside town on the Isle of Wight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sauce' tempts as food; it is the cheek sense, giving LIP.
explanation.definitionFit: Lip salve is an ointment for chapped lips, and an emollient is a softening cream.

clue.text: Rather wooden last night in Edinburgh?

parts.note: 'Rather!' is an old exclamation of agreement, like yes
treen means made of wood, especially small turned household items

explanation.surface: Someone recalls a rather stiff performance the previous evening in Scotland's capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rather' as an exclamation of strong agreement ('Rather!') gives YES; treen is wooden ware.
explanation.definitionFit: Yestreen is a Scots word for yesterday evening, hence the Scottish city in the question.

clue.text: Comparatively pathetic, the setter playing a character "at rest"

parts.note: the setter refers to himself as me
as means in the role of, as when an actor plays as someone
a lier is one who lies down, so one at rest

explanation.surface: The setter, cast in a part as someone resting, admits to being rather feeble.
explanation.definitionFit: Measly means paltry or pitiful, and the comparative form describes something even more meagre.

clue.text: From within, Paris enclave originated …

indicators.note: From within says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Something has emerged from inside a quarter of the French capital, the ellipsis carrying the thought onward.
explanation.definitionFit: To have arisen is to have come into being or sprung up, which is to have originated.

clue.text: … every Adamic convention

indicators.note: Adam went naked in Eden, so Adamic means stripped of the outer letters that clothe the word

parts.note: a rally is a mass gathering or convention

explanation.surface: Continuing from the previous clue: every custom going back to Adam.
explanation.walkthrough: Adam was the first naturist, so the convention RALLY loses its 'clothing', its first and last letters.
explanation.definitionFit: All and every both mean each one without exception, as in all or every member present.

clue.text: Fanciful banshees? They're so passe!

indicators.note: fanciful means imaginative or invented, so the letters are rearranged freely

explanation.surface: Imaginary wailing spirits from Irish folklore are declared hopelessly out of fashion.
explanation.definitionFit: Has-beens are people whose fame or usefulness is over, which is to be out of date.

clue.text: Unaware of son entering game

indicators.note: entering means the son's letter goes inside the game

parts.note: lotto is a game of chance like bingo
S is the genealogical abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: Someone does not realise their boy has joined in a game.
explanation.definitionFit: To be lost to something is to be insensible to it, no longer noticing it.

clue.text: Left-winger's jumping well over tall ref

indicators.note: jumping means leaping about, so the letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A left-wing player hops easily over a tall referee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Left-winger' suggests a footballer on the left flank; it is a political sympathiser.
explanation.definitionFit: A fellow traveller is a sympathiser with communism who is not a party member, so a left-winger.

clue.text: Perhaps Leman's a non-com at Coningsby?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: lake in French, as in ... Léman, the French name for Lake Geneva
second meaning: Leading Aircraftman, a junior non-commissioned RAF rank; Coningsby is an RAF station in Lincolnshire

explanation.walkthrough: 'Leman' looks like an old word for a lover or a surname; it is Lake Geneva, which the French call Lac Léman.
explanation.definitionFit: The French word for lake names Lake Geneva, and the RAF abbreviation names an airman of low rank.

clue.text: Bobby's coming back strongly — duck!

indicators.note: coming back means the word for the policeman is read in reverse

parts.note: a bobby is a British police officer, a cop
hard means with force, strongly

explanation.surface: A police officer returns forcefully, so someone shouts to take cover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'duck!' reads as a warning to dodge; it is the bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The pochard is a diving duck with a chestnut head, found across Europe.

clue.text: Set in concrete, MOD office backing measure

indicators.note: backing means the hidden letters are read in the reverse direction
set in means the letters sit inside the run of words that follows

parts.note: the letters run from the end of concrete through MOD into office

explanation.surface: A Ministry of Defence department is fixed firmly, a measure supporting it.
explanation.walkthrough: MOD is the UK Ministry of Defence.
explanation.definitionFit: An odometer is an instrument that records distance travelled, so a measuring device.

clue.text: Indifferent hypodermics (new) replaced by hospital on basis of infectiousness

indicators.note: replaced by means the letter for new gives way to the letter for hospital

parts.note: hypodermics are hypodermic needles
H is the map abbreviation for hospital

indicators.note: the basis is the bottom, so the last letter of the word is taken

explanation.surface: Uncaring medical staff swap needles at a hospital, unbothered about infection risk.
explanation.definitionFit: Heedless means paying no attention, careless, which is to be unconcerned or indifferent.

clue.text: Oscar runs banks in part of France

parts.note: Oscar is O in the NATO phonetic alphabet
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs
an aircraft banks when it leans or tilts

explanation.surface: A man called Oscar sprints along riverbanks somewhere in France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'banks' looks like riverbanks or money; it is the tilting sense, LEANS.
explanation.definitionFit: Orléans is a city on the Loire, and the Orléanais was a historic province of France.

clue.text: Since losing exceptional singer Georgians falter

indicators.note: losing says letters go, and exceptional says they go in any order, not as a run
falter means stumble, so the letters that remain are muddled

explanation.surface: A people from Georgia stumble after their outstanding vocalist leaves.
explanation.walkthrough: Strike the letters of SINGER from GEORGIANS, in any order, leaving G, O, A, then rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Ago means in the past, before now, as in 'long ago', the sense of 'since' in 'long since'.

clue.text: Foodie's impressive puree — with nothing superficial

parts.note: epic means grand or impressive

indicators.note: nothing on the surface means the outer letters are stripped from the word

explanation.surface: A food lover praises a magnificent puree with no shallow touches.
explanation.definitionFit: An epicure is a person with refined taste in food and drink, a gourmet.

clue.text: Behave tediously in Brent teashop, perhaps?

parts.note: read the answer as an instruction: an anagram of BORE THE PANTS, signalled by OFF, makes these two words

explanation.surface: Being thoroughly dull in a cafe in Brent, a London borough.
explanation.walkthrough: This is a reverse anagram: the answer's last word is the anagram signal and its first three words rearrange to make the clue's two words.
explanation.definitionFit: To bore the pants off someone is an idiom for wearying them utterly with dullness.

clue.text: Leak on board spreads swiftly

indicators.note: on here means aboard, so the leaking word sits inside the ship

parts.note: being on board means being on a ship, and SS is the usual steamship abbreviation
to weep is to ooze or leak liquid

explanation.surface: Water seeping into a ship quickly moves through the vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: SS, for steamship, is the crossword's usual ship.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that sweeps through a place moves across it rapidly, as a fire or rumour does.

clue.text: Loaded vans of food and tackle, checking all tyres

indicators.note: the van is the front, so vans of means the first letter of each word

explanation.surface: Vehicles laden with food and gear, someone inspecting every tyre.
explanation.definitionFit: A fat cat is a wealthy, privileged person, and loaded means rich in slang.

clue.text: Wizard engine

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the magician of Arthurian legend
second meaning: the Rolls-Royce aero engine that powered the Spitfire

explanation.walkthrough: One name covers King Arthur's enchanter and a famous wartime aircraft power unit.
explanation.definitionFit: The Arthurian magician and the Rolls-Royce aero engine share the same name.

clue.text: Recording unit reconnoitre around burrow

indicators.note: around means the scouting word wraps the burrow

parts.note: to case a place is to scout it before a crime
a sett is a badger's burrow

explanation.surface: A tape recorder scouts out an animal's den.
explanation.definitionFit: A cassette is a sealed case of magnetic tape used for recording sound or video.

clue.text: Butcher regularly flipped old coin

indicators.note: flipped means the chosen letters are turned the other way round
regularly means every other letter of the word is taken

explanation.surface: A meat seller tosses an antique coin over and over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flipped' and 'coin' suggest tossing a coin; flipped reverses the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The écu was an old French coin, first minted in gold under Louis IX.

clue.text: Instead of poetry, university goes in for the more recent English

indicators.note: goes in for means one letter takes the place of the other

parts.note: verses are poetry
E is the abbreviation for English, and the more recent one is the later of the two in the word

explanation.surface: A university swaps poetry for modern English literature.
explanation.definitionFit: Versus means as opposed to or as an alternative to, close to 'in place of'.

clue.text: Train dramatically let off steam after rumble heard

indicators.note: after means the word for letting off steam is placed following the sound of the rumble
heard means the word is spoken aloud and only its sound counts

parts.note: a roll is a rumbling sound, as of thunder or drums
to play is to relax and let off steam

explanation.surface: A train lets off steam after a rumble is heard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Train' looks like a railway engine letting off steam; it is the verb to rehearse, ROLE-PLAY.
explanation.definitionFit: Role-play is acting out a scenario to practise skills, a form of training by acting.
